_schema: technologies/areas: [{id,label,description,aliases[],patterns[],topics[],lang[],lang_weight,exclude[],exclude_topics[],contextual[],from_tech[],implies[],readme_min,min_score,embed_min,require_focus,fallback,children[]}]. Rules score evidence per field and assign a node at score >= min_score (default _rules.min_score per dimension). aliases: case-insensitive whole-word phrases ('-'/'_' read as spaces) matched in the repo name (weight name), description (description; +1 when two different aliases hit, +no_readme when the entry has no README), item names/descriptions (items; 1 when only one of many items hits) and README (readme when >= readme_min mentions, readme_single for fewer; technologies use readme_tech; readme_min 0 disables README). topics: GitHub topics that count as topic evidence; multi-word aliases also match topics, single-word aliases do not. patterns: case-sensitive regexes, same fields as aliases. lang: GitHub primaryLanguage values (lang_weight, default weights.language; 1 for content packs such as skill/agent/prompt collections). exclude: case-insensitive regexes blanked from every text before matching. exclude_topics: the node is never assigned when the repo has one of these topics. contextual: aliases that count for a child only when its parent scored on its own. from_tech: technology ids that add weights.tech to an area. implies: sibling ids assigned with this node; a child always implies its parent. Sub-entries (id != repo) use only their own name/description/items. description drives embeddings; embed_min is written by classify.py --calibrate. require_focus: N means topic/items/README evidence only counts when the name or description also names the node or the README mentions it N+ times. fallback: true marks the general-purpose node, never matched by rules or embeddings; repos left without tags in a dimension get it (evidence method 'fallback'), except archived repos and entries with neither description nor README. platform: true for tools an extension works inside (Figma, WordPress...): built-with phrases such as 'a Figma plugin' are not blanked for these nodes.
